name: Fixer (Basic Councelor)

currentBonuses.when: while this counselor is hired, to Impersonate or Lie with people inside their location
while this counselor is hired, to Make an Impression or Request with people inside their location

evidence: A counselor automatically Aids you on attempts to Impersonate, Lie, Make an Impression, and Request when speaking with individuals within the location of the counselor's expertise.

corrections.problem: The evidence quoted does not contain the bonus size claimed. The quoted sentence is "A counselor automatically Aids you on attempts to Impersonate, Lie, Make an Impression, and Request when speaking with individuals within the location of the counselor's expertise" — it names no number. Verified against the record: the words '+1 circumstance bonus' appear ONLY in the informant paragraph ('An informant automatically Aids you... granting you a +1 circumstance bonus to such checks'); the counselor paragraph gives a number only for the EXPERT counselor (+2). The engineNote's claim that '+1 comes from the shared Fixer text' is therefore an inference from Aid's default success result, not a quote, yet the spec is filed confidence:'high', needsHumanDecision:false.
corrections.correction: Keep the +1 circumstance value (it is Aid's printed success result and is consistent with the expert's +2), but stop presenting it as quoted. Either widen the evidence to include the informant sentence and say explicitly 'value inferred from Aid's success entry / the parallel informant clause', or drop confidence to medium. No change to the targets: Impersonate + Lie = deception, Make an Impression + Request = diplomacy, both verified correct.

corrections.problem: The batch answers its own open question inconsistently. skeptics-elixir sets needsHumanDecision:true asking whether an undrunk consumable should light a star, and explicitly says 'This decides skeptics-elixir, ichthyosis-mutagen, fungal-walk-musk and every other consumable in this batch' — yet all five of those records are filed needsHumanDecision:false. All are verified consumables in core.json (itemType 'consumable' with uses {current:1,max:1} for skeptics-elixir-*, ichthyosis-mutagen and fungal-walk-musk), so the same unresolved policy governs them.
corrections.correction: Propagate needsHumanDecision:true (with the same question text) to every consumable record in the batch, or resolve the policy once and set it false everywhere. The bonus values themselves need no change. Note that the Will-save half of the elixir carries no condition beyond the duration — if the app ever models drunk consumables as an active effect/Mode, that half must move out of the star registry into the maths for its duration, and the star must not be left behind or it will double-count.

Crimson Fulcrum Lens invested and the melee Strike is a jaws attack

for 1 minute after spending an Ebon Fulcrum Lens glimmer (or for 24 hours after rejuvenating with one)
for 1 minute after spending an Ebon Fulcrum Lens glimmer (or for 24 hours after rejuvenating with one)
for 1 minute after spending an Ebon Fulcrum Lens glimmer (or for 24 hours after rejuvenating with one)

evidence: Crimson: "You gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against fear effects"; Ochre: "You gain resistance 10 to mental damage and a +2 status bonus to saves against emotion effects"; Ebon: "you gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and DCs"; Emerald: "gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against magic for 1 round".

corrections.problem: Two target-precision defects. (a) The Ebon lens grants '+1 item bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and DCs' (verified in both the umbrella and ebon-fulcrum-lens). The spec maps 'DCs' to classDc only and relegates the spell DC to a prose note — but 'spell' is an available target kind, so the second half is simply omitted rather than unrepresentable. (b) The Emerald entry '+4 status ... to the Hit Points harm spells restore to you' is filed against targetKind 'hp'. Verified text: 'harm spells gain a +4 status bonus to the Hit Points they restore to you' — that is a bonus to healing RECEIVED, not to the Hit Points stat; starring the HP tile implies a bigger HP pool.
corrections.correction: (a) Add a parallel entry { bonus: '+1 item', when: '<same Ebon glimmer condition>', targetKind: 'spell' } alongside the classDc entry. (b) Keep the hp entry only if the engineNote names the gap explicitly — there is no 'healing received' lane, so hp is an approximation, and the 'when' must lead with 'to the Hit Points a Harm spell restores to you' so no reader mistakes it for extra max HP. Everything else on this record checks out, including the deliberate exclusions (Crimson's flat +2 melee Strike damage, Ochre's resistance 10 mental, Ebon's incorporeal/drained 2, Emerald's void healing) and the crimson-fulcrum-lens observation that core.json types the existing strikeDamage entry 'untyped' while the text says ITEM bonus — that data discrepancy is real and worth a separate fix ticket.

name: Spellcutter

currentBonuses.when: against a spell that targets you, when you spend the reaction while wielding Spellcutter
against a spell that targets you, when you spend the reaction while wielding Spellcutter

evidence: "**Trigger** You're targeted by a spell while wielding *Spellcutter* **Effect** *Spellcutter* attempts to absorb the magic of the triggering spell, giving you a +4 status bonus to your AC and saves against the effect."

corrections.problem: The spec discards the item's defining mechanic — "an ancient restriction on the blade prevents it from harming living creatures; attacks against living beings deal no damage" — with the reason "that is a damage nullification, not a typed penalty, so it has no target kind." That reason is factually wrong about the registry. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts documents the bonus field as "The modifier, e.g. '+1 circumstance', or a short effect phrase", and already ships non-numeric and NEGATIVE entries: line 69 "barbarian-dedication": bonus "-1 (penalty)"; line 329 "terrain-scout": bonus "ally benefit (no roll bonus)". strikeDamage is exactly the right target kind, and this is a conditional, per-Strike effect on the character's own damage. Dropping it means a player wielding a cursed unique weapon gets no marker for the one thing that will most surprise them mid-combat.
corrections.correction: Add a third entry to spellcutter alongside the two +4 status ones: { bonus: 'no damage (cursed)', when: 'on Strikes against living creatures — the blade deals no damage to them; dhampirs and creatures with Void Healing are exempt and take damage normally', target: { kind: 'strikeDamage' } }. Keep situational:true and drop the "has no target kind" claim from the engineNote.

name: Noqual Armor

currentBonuses.when: against spell attack rolls, while wearing the noqual armor

evidence: "While wearing noqual armor, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against spell attack rolls."

corrections.problem: Two problems, both silent decisions that were not escalated. (1) The spec asserts "The +4 material save (from the parent 'noqual' record) is not restated here, so it is not claimed on this record" — yet the record's own text does say "Base Material Noqual", and a suit of noqual armor is by definition an object made of noqual. Meanwhile the SAME batch claims that +4 on noqual-chunk, noqual-ingot and both noqual-object grades and escalates the question there. The result is backwards: a lump of ore in your backpack gets a starred save, and the armor you are actually wearing (the only noqual object a 'save to protect the item from magic' will realistically ever be rolled for) does not. (2) The DC 5 flat-check drawback is dismissed as having no target kind, on the same mistaken premise as spellcutter.
corrections.correction: (1) Either escalate the +4 owner-protection save on the equippable noqual records too, or — better, and my recommendation — invert the current split: put the +4 on noqual-armor / noqual-armor-standard-grade / noqual-armor-high-grade / noqual-shield family / noqual-weapon family, and drop it from noqual-chunk, noqual-ingot, noqual-object-standard-grade, noqual-object-high-grade (raw stock you never make a save to protect). Whatever is chosen must be applied to all nine records consistently. (2) Add { bonus: 'DC 5 flat check or the spell fails', when: 'whenever you Cast a Spell while wearing noqual armor', target: { kind: 'spell' } } — the registry's prose/penalty precedent (barbarian-dedication line 69) supports it, and a caster in noqual armor needs that flag more than the +1 AC. Applies identically to noqual-armor-standard-grade and noqual-armor-high-grade.

name: Noqual Buckler (High-Grade)

currentBonuses.when: against spells that target you, while this noqual buckler is Raised

evidence: "When you have a noqual shield Raised, you gain its circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells that target you (as well as AC)."

corrections.problem: The spec hard-codes bonus "+1 circumstance" and correctly admits "the record itself never prints a number ('its circumstance bonus')", then escalates it as a human decision. But the decision is already settled by existing practice in the file the spec is matching: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts line 221 "necromantic-deflection" uses exactly this construction — bonus: "shield's circumstance bonus" — for the identical rules pattern (raised shield lending its AC bonus to saves). Inventing a number the source text does not print, when the registry has a precedent for not doing so, is the avoidable error here.
corrections.correction: Replace the hard-coded number with the prose form used elsewhere in the registry: bonus: "buckler's circumstance bonus" (or "shield's circumstance bonus" to match necromantic-deflection verbatim), keep when: "against spells that target you, while this noqual buckler is Raised", target { kind: 'save', save: 'all' }. Set needsHumanDecision false and cite situationalBonuses.ts:221 as the precedent.

name: Noqual Shield (High-Grade)

currentBonuses.when: against spells that target you, while this noqual shield is Raised

evidence: "When you have a noqual shield Raised, you gain its circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells that target you (as well as AC)."

corrections.problem: Same defect as noqual-buckler-high-grade: bonus is hard-coded "+2 circumstance" while the spec concedes the record "never prints a number", and the question is escalated even though situationalBonuses.ts:221 ("necromantic-deflection": bonus "shield's circumstance bonus") already answers it. Hard-coding also silently assumes the underlying shield is a standard +2 shield, but 'Noqual Shield' is a base-MATERIAL record applicable to any shield the character actually equips.
corrections.correction: Use bonus: "shield's circumstance bonus" rather than "+2 circumstance"; keep when: "against spells that target you, while this noqual shield is Raised", target { kind: 'save', save: 'all' }. Set needsHumanDecision false, referencing situationalBonuses.ts:221. Note the umbrella noqual-shield record already uses a prose form and is fine as-is.

name: Exploration Lens (Investigating)

currentBonuses.when: on Recall Knowledge checks made while using the Investigate exploration activity, with the lens activated

evidence: "While activated, the lens grants you a +1 item bonus to skill checks to Recall Knowledge while Investigating"

corrections.problem: needsEngineWork is set to true, but nothing on this record needs engine work for the situational-bonus feature. The spec's own engineNote concedes "The +1 itself maps cleanly to skills" and that the blocker is the clause "you can always roll a Recall Knowledge skill check appropriate to the investigation for initiative" — then adds "it also isn't a bonus". Per the task's own definition, needsEngineWork is for a BONUS whose target the app cannot express. An initiative-roll SUBSTITUTION is a permission, not a bonus, so nothing here is blocked. Leaving the flag true puts this record on an engine-work backlog it does not belong on (a false positive is as costly as a miss when the list is used to scope work).
corrections.correction: Set needsEngineWork false. Keep the single bonus entry unchanged (+1 item, when: 'on Recall Knowledge checks made while using the Investigate exploration activity, with the lens activated', target { kind: 'skill', skill: 'all' }), and demote the initiative-substitution clause to a prose/engineNote observation rather than a blocking flag.

name: Metronomic Hammer

currentBonuses.bonus: +1 item (rising to +2, then +3, on repeat Trips against the same target this turn)
currentBonuses.when: on Athletics checks to Trip with the hammer, after using its free-triggered activation; resets to +1 if you succeed, critically fail, or your turn ends

evidence: "you gain a +1 item bonus to your Athletics check to Trip the target… increases by 1 with every subsequent Trip attempt… to a maximum of +3"

corrections.problem: The player-facing condition calls the activation a "free-triggered activation". It is a REACTION, not a free action: the record has activationCost {type:'reaction'} and the description shows the reaction glyph ("**Activate** ⟨5⟩ envision"). Telling a player at the table that it costs nothing is an action-economy error — it consumes their reaction for the round, which usually means they only get one Trip bonus per round from it, not one per Trip attempt. (The same engineer labelled metuaks-pendant's identical ⟨5⟩ activation correctly as 'the pendant's reaction'.)
corrections.correction: Change the 'when' to: 'on Athletics checks to Trip with the hammer, after spending your reaction to envision its metronome; rises to +2 then +3 on repeat Trips against the same target this turn, and resets to +1 if you succeed, critically fail, or your turn ends'. The +1/+2/+3 ladder, the item type, and the athletics target are all correct.

name: Spiderfoot Brew

currentBonuses.when: to Athletics checks to Climb, while the brew lasts (lesser: 1 minute)

evidence: "granting you a climb Speed and an item bonus to Athletics checks made to Climb for the listed duration" — Lesser: "the climb Speed is 15 feet, the item bonus is +1, and the duration is 1 minute."

corrections.problem: The spec's whole basis is false. It claims "this record is the AoN family/stub entry ... level 3 matches the Lesser, so I specified +1". core.json ALSO contains spiderfoot-brew-lesser (lvl 3, 12 gp, "a climb Speed of 15 feet and a +1 item bonus to athletics checks made to climb for 1 minute"), spiderfoot-brew-moderate (lvl 9, 150 gp, +2/10 min) and spiderfoot-brew-greater (lvl 17, 2500 gp, +3/1 hour). So the bare `spiderfoot-brew` record is NOT the Lesser grade — it is a pure family/summary record whose text bundles all three grades, and its level 3 is just the family's minimum level. Pinning it to +1 is a guess presented as a grade match, and it silently under-reports the Moderate/Greater cases.
corrections.correction: Keep situational:true and the target (skill/athletics, item bonus, "to Athletics checks made to Climb while the brew lasts"), but the family record's bonus is grade-dependent: phrase it "+1 to +3 item (varies by grade)" — or, better, drop the family record from the registry entirely and register the three real graded records instead: spiderfoot-brew-lesser +1 item (1 minute), spiderfoot-brew-moderate +2 item (10 minutes), spiderfoot-brew-greater +3 item (1 hour). The spec's engineNote caveat (1) should be deleted, not asked as an open question — the graded records exist and answer it. The climb-Speed note and the consumable needsHumanDecision question are both fine.

name: Ridill

corrections.problem: needsHumanDecision:true with the question "Does the situational registry's `save` target accept 'all', or must every save bonus be pinned to fortitude/reflex/will?" — that question is already answered in the code the spec was matching. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts documents SituationalTarget.detail as "For `save`: `fortitude` | `reflex` | `will` | `all`", and targetMatches() implements `t.detail === 'all'` as a wildcard. Raising it as a blocker sends the app owner a decision that does not exist.
corrections.correction: Keep the bonuses exactly as specified (+2 circumstance to saves vs fear while wielding Ridill; +4 if the fear effect is from a dragon — both verified verbatim in the record) with save 'all', and set needsHumanDecision:false. The same spurious doubt is echoed in the grisantian-pelt-armor engineNote ('same save: all caveat as Ridill') and should be dropped there too — save 'all' is a first-class value, already used by affliction-resistance, adaptive-vision, aegis-of-the-dissolution and others.

name: Sprite Apple

currentBonuses.when: while in the apple's bright light (10 minutes) — Chartreuse apple only
to Diplomacy checks against animals or plants, while in the apple's bright light — Chartreuse apple only, and only if you have Animal Empathy, Plant Empathy, or a similar ability

evidence: "These bombs grant a +2 item bonus to attack rolls and deal 3d6 poison damage… If the primary target is under the effects of a morph or polymorph effect, it must succeed at a saving throw"

corrections.problem: needsEngineWork is set false on the strength of 'the bomb's own +2 item bonus to attack rolls … belongs in the strike maths (weapon item bonus)'. Verified in code: derive.ts:1188 computes the strike attack item bonus as Math.max(abpOn(c) ? abpAttack(c.level) : runes?.potency ?? 0, mpRef?.attack ?? 0) — i.e. only potency runes, ABP, or a Monster-Parts refine. The core.json record has no field carrying the printed item bonus (only damage/dice/range/group), so the +2 is currently dropped entirely rather than 'in the maths'. The skunk-bomb specs in the same chunk flagged this same gap as needsEngineWork true, so the two bomb families are classified inconsistently.
corrections.correction: situational stays false and bonuses stays empty (the classification is right — the bonus is unconditional for this bomb's Strike), but set needsEngineWork true with: 'Alchemical bomb item bonuses to attack rolls have no home in the engine — derive.ts sources the strike attack item bonus only from potency runes / ABP / Monster-Parts, and core.json bomb records carry no field for the printed +2. Needs an item-level attack-item-bonus field, not a situational star.'

name: Egg Cream Fizz

currentBonuses.when: to all your Speeds for 10 minutes after drinking (no further condition — this one is scope-unconditional while the elixir lasts)
to Balance, Maneuver in Flight, and Squeeze — only if the fizz was made with Chocolate syrup
to Climb, Leap, and Swim — only if the fizz was made with Strawberry syrup

evidence: "gaining a +5-foot item bonus to your Speed for 10 minutes… **Chocolate** You gain a +1 item bonus to Acrobatics checks to Balance, Maneuver in Flight, and Squeeze. **Strawberry** You gain a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks to Climb, Leap, and Swim."

corrections.problem: The Speed entry's condition broadens the text. The record says 'gaining a +5-foot item bonus to your Speed for 10 minutes'; the spec renders it as 'to all your Speeds for 10 minutes after drinking'. In PF2e a bonus to 'your Speed' is the land Speed unless it says 'all your Speeds', so this would wrongly buff fly/swim/burrow Speeds.
corrections.correction: Change the Speed entry's when to 'to your Speed (land Speed only — the text says "your Speed", not "all your Speeds") for 10 minutes after drinking'. The two syrup entries (Acrobatics to Balance/Maneuver in Flight/Squeeze for Chocolate; Athletics to Climb/Leap/Swim for Strawberry), the needsEngineWork flag and the human-decision question are all correct as written and should stand.
